editorial.headline: Alcohol Retail, Where the Sale Ends Before the Drink Begins
editorial.standfirst: Specialist retail of alcoholic drinks spans every listed business scale, but foreign-investment access in Bali turns on the exact declared scope and its OSS risk.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is specialist retail of alcoholic beverages for consumption elsewhere, rather than drinks served to be consumed where they are bought. Its territory is broad in format while remaining precise in purpose: spirits such as whisky, brandy, gin, arak, rum and sake; wine; and malt-based drinks including beer, ale and stout all sit within the stated scope. The retail sale may take place indoors, at roadside stalls, from shop-front verandas, in movable market spaces, through other media, or online. The record also expressly includes alcohol retailers in duty-free shops and retailers of Group B and C alcoholic beverages.

The activity is available to micro, small, medium and large businesses. That breadth of scale should not be mistaken for a simple national foreign-investment invitation. Nationally, the PMA position is recorded as restricted, with the foreign-ownership setting described as “special” rather than expressed as a general percentage ceiling. The supplied reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In practical editorial terms, this is a retail activity with a clearly defined commercial subject, but a national PMA status that requires it to be read as restricted rather than assumed to be fully foreign-open.

Bali introduces a narrower, scope-sensitive distinction. The record does not say that PMA registration is blocked outright for this activity in Bali. Instead, it says the outcome depends on the scope declared. At the large-business scale, OSS risk is low for some scopes and higher for others. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; for this record, PMA registration in Bali is available only when the higher-risk scope is declared. The conclusion is therefore neither a blanket refusal nor an automatic approval. For a founder seeking PMA registration, the decisive issue is the exact scope declared and its live OSS risk classification.
